set.body:
Phase: core. Track: engine.

Outcome
One table-driven test proves what each kind of caller can and cannot see through every route that returns data.

Acceptance
1. Rows are the read routes, including the new ones: release, metadata, file, export, selections, catalog record, search, shares, grants, access explanation, readiness, labs and projects.
2. Columns are the caller's standing: no access; knows it exists; reads metadata; reads content; fixed release only; project member; steward; expired grant; revoked grant; disabled account.
3. Each cell states the expected outcome and the visible fields. It is written by hand from the policy, not derived from the implementation. Canary values in hidden releases, hidden projects and hidden columns never appear in any response, count or page boundary.
4. The matrix runs through HTTP against both the reference and the PostgreSQL catalogs, and in hosted CI.
5. A new read route cannot be added without a row: the test fails on a route that has none.

Start from
- modules/integration/src/test/scala/sanctity/postgres/DisclosureSuite.scala.
- The access matrix in the frozen workload (docs/engineering-workload.md).
- modules/http/src/main/scala/sanctity/http/RepositoryHttp.scala: the dispatcher.

Evidence
The matrix file and its CI job.
set.title: CORE5: Access matrix: every read route against every level of access
